title: Three Springs and One Short Trowel
subtitle: 植物农业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）
meta: 主题语境：植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）　|　核心词汇：tomato　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 tomato 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1974 the gardener ① picked the tomato that no apprentice in the garden would have recorded, and he said the picking was the whole of the spring. The ② tomato, meaning the vegetable itself and not the trowel, ran three springs and stayed unrecorded in the book; a tomato, he said, is the only thing in a garden that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ tomato in that garden had the same short trowel beside it, and the ④ tomato at the far bed, meaning the cutting they kept for the children to plant and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A tomato, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the gardener said the recording is the part that fills three springs.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the tomato was the whole of the matter, meaning the freshness and not the vegetable. The ⑥ tomato, meaning the freshness and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; tomato, he said, is either something you pick or the only word that means both a vegetable and a freshness. He said the freshness is the part they remember.

By 1979 the ⑦ tomato had become a line in a notebook, and the notebook had become an argument about the short trowel. The ⑧ tomato of the whole thing, the gardener wrote in April, was one garden and three springs of recording; tomato, he said, is either the cutting at the far bed or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ tomato I remember is the vegetable recorded in the notebook, which closed in 1981 and is still recorded as the quietest in the garden. A ⑩ tomato, my mother said in 1983, is the only vegetable that improves by being recorded; every tomato, she said, is a freshness that has agreed to look like a vegetable. She said the freshness was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 西红柿；番茄（指园子里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 西红柿；番茄（指那个西红柿本身，与小小的花铲相对）
C. 固定搭配：pick the tomato 摘这一个西红柿
D. n. 西红柿；番茄（指留给孩子们插的那一枝）
E. n. 西红柿之事（抽象总称，指一处园子的西红柿之事）
F. n. 西红柿；番茄（指园艺笔记里写到、被记载的那一个）
G. n. 西红柿、鲜亮（指一件事里人人都种却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 鲜亮（抽象总称，指人人都种却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: picked the tomato that no apprentice in the garden would have recorded

answers.why: pick the tomato 意为“摘这一个西红柿”，1974 年那位园丁把园子里没有一位学徒肯记载的一个西红柿做了一遍。
tomato 意为“西红柿；番茄”，指那个西红柿本身而不是小小的花铲，它经过了三个春天而在簿子上没有被记载。
tomato 意为“西红柿；番茄”，指园子里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一把小小的花铲。
tomato 意为“西红柿；番茄”，指最远那畦苗床的留给孩子们插的那一枝，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
tomato 意为“西红柿、鲜亮”，指一件事里人人都种却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个鲜亮就是那件事的全部。
tomato 意为“鲜亮”，指人人都种却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个西红柿，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
tomato 意为“西红柿；番茄”，指园艺笔记里写到、被记载的那一个，到 1979 年这一个成了园艺笔记里的一行。
tomato 意为“西红柿之事”，园丁四月写道，整件事的西红柿之事是一处园子和三个春天的记载。
tomato 意为“西红柿；番茄”，我记得的是园艺笔记里记载过的那一个，1981 年栽完了，至今仍被说成园子里最安静的一个。
tomato 为抽象总称，母亲 1983 年说，西红柿是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的西红柿。
